approach.method_basis: The Parent starts from the best supplied molecule and samples local atom, bond, path and ring edits, including a direct exchange of aromatic nitrogen and carbon that preserves molecular formula. It normalizes molecular identities, rejects duplicates and submits the first full batch admitted by its structural memory. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next current molecule even after a tie or loss, while a separate archive keeps the best observation. Every selected transition currently installs short-lived inverse motif restrictions, regardless of whether that transition improved its source. A later neighbor is vetoed when opposite signed restrictions match the same earlier transition.
approach.novelty: Give new memory credit only to a selected transition that strictly improves its actual source score. Tied and worsening winners still become current and age existing memory, but install or refresh no restrictions. This tests whether protecting locally unsuccessful moves unnecessarily blocks fresh variations that reverse their motifs. Earlier siblings refined which motif matches cause a veto, repaired identity bookkeeping, changed local chemistry or reweighted edit operators; none conditioned restriction installation on the individual selected winner's observed gain. The Parent's aromatic nitrogen exchange remains part of the tested method.

observed_bottleneck: Parent n-abcd951ab7cc completes its supplied panel at macro mean 0.5217591163770486 and population deviation 0.006329100643035156, with paired gain 0.0008412882577690054 over n-9f7c7ec50039. Its recorded 435 selected transitions comprise 257 improvements, 49 ties and 129 losses, yet all receive the same inverse-installation treatment. Of 1711 installed attributes, 194 originate from tied moves and 508 from worsening moves. Among 4545 valid novel attempts, 195 are vetoed: 115 by improving-transition groups, 17 by tied-transition groups and 63 by worsening-transition groups. Thus 80 actual vetoes protect transitions that did not improve their source. An unscored chronological replay of the recorded Parent history with the proposed installation gate retains 1009 installations, skips 702 and changes vetoes from 195 to 116. It admits 79 formerly vetoed draws, representing 74 distinct identities within batches across 62 batches, with no newly vetoed draw in this recorded stream. Twelve skipped overlaps preserve an older improving restriction, explaining why this replay differs from simply removing the 80 nonimproving-origin vetoes. These are opportunity measurements on the fixed recorded history, not an alternative evaluated trajectory. The earlier n-d88727c16484 established that more selective memory changes real evaluation allocation while leaving the value of its surviving vetoes unresolved. The failed operator-weighting sibling n-9ab62999124d also shows why more source-improvement events alone cannot establish better final search quality.
hypothesis: Install and refresh inverse-motif restrictions only when the selected actually accepted neighbor has a strictly higher score than its recorded source; tied and worsening selected transitions still move and age the walk but receive no new memory credit.

finding_summary.headline: Selective memory credit admitted 74 scored neighbors, but lowered the panel mean
finding_summary.insights: The experiment establishes that protecting nonimproving moves can block useful fresh variations: newly admitted methyl removal and aryl-fluorine removal both produced immediate archive gains. It also rules out an unexercised gate, missing feedback or changed restriction tenure as explanations for the negative panel result. Those useful cases were sparse, and overall source-improvement frequency and positive-gain magnitude fell. The archive improved slightly more often, but its total improvement was smaller. This narrows the question to the search value of the restrictions: withholding credit based on one move's local gain does not reliably identify protection that is expendable on this panel. Whether protecting nonimproving moves helps diversification remains unresolved because the passive comparison cannot reproduce an alternative walk or score excluded candidates. Preserved overlap provenance matters in practice: an older improving pair survived a skipped refresh and blocked a candidate that unconditional credit would admit. Thus the gate does not create a universal admissibility superset. The supplied molecular assessment still finds reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual sulfur connections and dense ring systems alongside recognizable aromatic/carbonyl and amine families; the changed allocation supplies no evidence that chemical feasibility improved.
finding_summary.results: All 184 tied or worsening selected moves skipped memory installation, omitting 719 attributes while retaining 984 attributes from improving moves. On the Child's recorded history, unconditional credit would veto 188 novel draws; the actual gate vetoed 115. This admitted 74 candidates across all fifteen task sessions, while preserved older provenance caused one additional veto in the opposite direction. Twenty newly admitted candidates became next states. Fourteen improved their source score, thirteen tied and forty-seven worsened it; only two immediately improved the archive. The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.501486, a paired change of -0.020273, against the registered requirement of +0.002. Two seeds declined and one improved. Task means improved for zaleplon and median_2, but declined for deco_hop, DRD2 and sitagliptin, with the largest loss in DRD2. All runs completed their full budgets and batches.

molecular.headline: Aromatic carbonyl and amine families persist, with small fused rings, reactive heteroatom bonds and sulfur-rich cages
molecular.overall_character: All supplied Child and Parent trajectory files were read; all five objectives are covered. Each Child task contains 900 recorded molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. Ring-closure and branch-token rates are 1.0 throughout. Aromatic-token rates are 0.9793, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 and 0.7839 in the supplied task order; mean SMILES lengths are 45.9, 68.6, 68.6, 61.8 and 63.4. These are substantial connected ring-bearing compounds, ranging from comparatively compact indole/carbonyl derivatives to bulky decorated aza-heterocycles, aryl polyamines, expanded heterocycles and densely connected sulfur cages. The token rates describe strings containing those features, not aromatic atom fractions or chemically perceived ring counts. Diversity is moderate across seeds and frameworks, but many leading examples are close local analogues. The chemistry changes relative to Parent n-abcd951ab7cc without resolving its recurring feasibility problems. Ordinary amides, ethers, amines and aromatic rings coexist with N-halogen and O-halogen bonds, peroxide connections, unusual sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds and demanding ring junctions. Every task has charge-token and stereocentre-token rates of 0.0; this leaves stereogenic relationships unspecified and does not imply that the amines cannot protonate. Apparent synthesis and medicinal quality are therefore questionable despite recognizable useful fragments. Score comparisons below are observations from the provided trajectories, not new scores, binding-mode assignments or claims about hidden objective requirements.

per_task.generated_character: The relatively compact leading molecules retain an aromatic core and a carbonyl connection to another aromatic ring. The strongest seed-2 example is a benzofuran-like system fused to a small saturated carbocycle bearing a primary amine, with a methyl group and an arylmethyl ketone whose terminal ring carries an N-chloro amino group. Seed 0 instead produces an ethoxy/methyl aromatic framework fused to small carbocycles, linked through an ordinary amide to an aminoaryl group; nearby variants contain benzothiophene or aza-aromatic rings and hydroxylamine functionality. Seed 1 retains an ethoxy/methyl/thiol indole carboxanilide. The latter has recognizable conventional synthetic connections, whereas the small fused rings and reactive substituents complicate other leaders. Lower examples replace the carbonyl connection with a saturated heteroatom-rich carbon, disrupt aromaticity or join a thioester to an expanded unsaturated sulfur ring. Late molecules retain the carbonyl families while adding further sulfur and N-O chemistry.
liabilities: N-Cl and N-O functionality introduces reactivity concerns distinct from ordinary carbon-bound halogens.
Small fused carbocycles and later densely connected sulfur-containing rings make strain and practical synthesis uncertain.
Free thiol and hydroxylamine functionality adds potential oxidation or metabolic liabilities in some otherwise recognizable aromatic carbonyl compounds.
missing_features: The weak carbonyl-replaced and ring-expanded derivatives lack the compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement present in the stronger families.
Stable matched analogues around the strongest small-ring and N-chloro structures remain incomplete, although a conventional indole amide already supports a nearby score.
Configurations at substituted saturated ring positions remain undefined; the strings do not establish feasible ring-junction geometry.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fused benzofuran arylmethyl ketone reaches 0.411894423222435, the small-carbocycle aryl amide 0.4083852185597655, and the ordinary indole carboxanilide 0.39905049777278273. The initial methoxy-substituted indole amide scores 0.3051048083696145. The carbonyl-replaced derivative scores 0.03343008011310944, while an expanded sulfur-ring thioester scores 0.011062485163751802. The stronger molecules therefore associate with compact aromatic/carbonyl organization; these are not isolated tests of every substituent. Conventional amide chemistry already supports a nearby strong score, so N-chlorination and unusual sulfur are not universal requirements of the observed high-score families. Relative to Parent, seed 0 changes from a benzothiophene-like aryl ketone at 0.393567030299894 to the fused small-carbocycle amide at 0.4083852185597655. Seed 2 changes from an N-chloro amide at 0.41003927643747895 to an N-chloro aminoaryl ketone at 0.411894423222435. The seed-1 indole leader and its score are unchanged.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family consists of bulky substituted aza-aromatics: a pyrazole-like ring connects a cyano-substituted amidine, an ester-bearing brominated aza-aryl ring with direct O-F functionality, and an alkyl-linked aza-aryl ring with a fluoromethyl ether. Alkyl and chloromethyl substitution on the amidine nitrogen varies. An oxygen-oxygen-fluorine derivative also appears near the top. The final seed-2 family is different: a fused nitrogen-rich dione is joined to an amino aza/ether ring carrying branched alkyl and O-S-methyl substitution, together with an unsaturated carbon chain. Low molecules retain recognizable ester, phenol and nitrogen/carbonyl fragments but alter or open their original ring connections. The ordinary ester and heteroaromatic fragments are plausible individually; reactive O-F/O-O bonds, flexible appendages and complex heteroatom linkages make the complete products less convincing.
liabilities: Direct O-F and O-O-F connections are reactive functionality; the fluoromethyl ether elsewhere is a different type of fluorine connection.
Chloromethyl amine substitution, O-S bonds and sulfur-rich alternatives raise stability concerns beyond the ordinary ester and aza-aromatic fragments.
Branched flexible side chains and unspecified alkene/imine geometry make the assembled molecular identity and synthesis less controlled.
missing_features: Low altered-ring derivatives lack the retained aromatic/heterocyclic connections present in the stronger decorated compounds.
A matched series replacing direct O-F and O-O functionality with stable connections while retaining the same attachment framework is incomplete.
Simplified appendage variants are incompletely explored despite exact ties across several amidine N-substituents; imine geometry and substituted side-chain configurations remain unspecified.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-chloromethyl, N-methyl and N-ethyl members of the leading amidine family all score 0.6057957681692732. A related O-O-F member remains close at 0.6051188299817185. Thus the recorded scores do not require chloromethyl substitution and discriminate poorly against the peroxide-containing appendage in this context. The initial aromatic dione scores 0.548381482770623; early altered-ring derivatives score 0.526081691583997 and 0.5286081645773063. The final seed-2 dione derivatives can retain 0.5999120578463943 despite changes in the unsaturated chain, whereas altered core-ring examples fall to 0.5450350272434115 and 0.541765876888247. This supports the decorated aromatic/heterocyclic organization more clearly than the necessity of each peripheral group. Parent seed 1 reaches 0.605139548855754 with a related amidine/thioester family; the Child uses an oxygen ester and altered side-chain substitution at 0.6057957681692732. The Parent seed-0 leader at 0.6161710037174721 contains a different heavily decorated thiocarbonyl/sulfur-linker family; the Child seed-0 maximum is 0.5954317897371715. Neither family establishes a clean chemical feasibility solution.

per_task.generated_character: The displayed strongest molecules are substantial aryl/polyamine compounds, with propyl and chloro substituents on an aromatic ring, a fluorinated saturated nitrogen ring attached to another chloroaryl or aza-aryl ring, and a primary aminomethyl group. A fused sulfur-rich ring framework connects these fragments and includes multiply bonded, additionally substituted sulfur and S-H-containing sulfur-sulfur connections. Other seeds explore phenolic aryl/amine compounds and constrained polyaryl nitrogen frameworks. The weak early compounds instead retain a carboxylic acid, amide and sulfonamide from the supplied biaryl scaffold. Aromatic and ring tokens occur in every proposal, and the halogen-token rate is 0.9977. The basic amine and aryl fragments are recognizable medicinal chemistry; the unusual sulfur framework and ring constraints make the assembled leaders questionable synthetic targets.
liabilities: Sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds and multiply bonded sulfur bearing additional ring connections are major stability and synthesis concerns.
Constrained saturated-ring junctions and substituted fluorinated carbons require defined spatial relationships.
Halogenated hydrophobic aromatic surface and several potential basic sites coexist without evidence about solubility or charge state.
missing_features: Low acid/amide/sulfonamide derivatives do not present the same accessible aliphatic amines and aryl/linker organization as the stronger polyamines.

Stable conventional-valence ring and linker alternatives preserving the stronger aryl/amine placement remain incomplete; the score tie shows that at least one extra sulfur substitution is optional locally.
The substituted fluorinated nitrogen ring and fused framework lack assigned configurations, and the neutral strings leave actual solution ionization unestablished.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The propyl/chloroaryl fluorinated-ring polyamine scores 0.9441493227693659, compared with 0.007468397818197266 for an early acid/amide/sulfonamide derivative. A close final molecule whose N-bound aromatic ring is contracted and dearomatized scores 0.31720419251336807. This supports the specific aryl/amine arrangement and ring geometry, rather than ring or nitrogen presence alone. A matched pair replacing a fused-ring carbon with sulfur both score 0.9440022868010379, so the additional sulfur at that position is not distinguished by the recorded score. The ethyl relative scores 0.937212258769855, and removal of the terminal aryl chlorine gives 0.9219399272276856. These smaller changes coexist with the much larger response to altering the N-bound aromatic ring. Parent seed 2 reaches 0.9148143511682032 with a phenolic aryl/polyamine/sulfur-ring family; the Child shifts its substituents and nitrogen-ring chemistry at 0.9441493227693659 while retaining unusual sulfur bonding. Child seed-0 and seed-1 maxima are 0.808939892923393 and 0.7239150289524697, versus Parent 0.8856242185485628 and 0.868020189804352; this chemistry change is not a uniform improvement across seeds.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-2 family contains sizeable expanded and interconnected N/O/S rings, a cyclic urea-like carbonyl unit and another ring carbonyl, a benzene ring and an alkoxy-substituted aza-aromatic ring. The strongest member carries an unusual substituted S-H centre and a multiply bonded sulfur ring connection. An earlier high molecule has an N-N connection in a related carbonyl/ether framework. Seed 1 instead retains a more aromatic nitrogen/carbonyl heterocycle flanked by alkyl/alkoxy aryl and haloaryl groups, with oxygenated sulfur-sulfur substitution. Seed 0 has a cyclic urea and ether-containing polycyclic aryl framework with an ester. Low examples open the carbonyl-containing heterocycle into a flexible chain, or disrupt the aromatic system while adding unusual sulfur and O-Br chemistry. The recognizable urea, ether and aromatic fragments do not establish straightforward synthesis of the expanded or tightly interconnected assemblies.
liabilities: Substituted S-H centres and unusual oxygenated sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds complicate stability and synthesis.
N-N links, oxygenated sulfur-sulfur groups and late O-Br substitution warrant chemical scrutiny rather than being interchangeable with ordinary carbon, ether or amide connections.
Expanded heterocycles and dense ring interconnections create substantial conformational and synthetic uncertainty.
missing_features: Low ring-opened molecules lack the constrained aromatic/carbonyl organization retained by stronger cyclic examples.
Matched ordinary-valence connections within the expanded and fused ring families remain incomplete, even where nitrogen/sulfur or sulfur-bond variants tie.
Stereochemical relationships and accessible conformations of the interconnected rings remain undefined; adding ring closures alone does not establish better geometry.

Ring-opened carbonyl-chain molecules score 0.12467972074136988 and 0.1263981386214515, supporting retained cyclic aromatic/carbonyl organization. Another pair changing the propyl-bearing ring nitrogen to an S-H centre both score 0.1996542320706886. Thus several chemically consequential atom/bond changes are score-indistinguishable locally. Parent seed 0 reaches 0.21196904390980506 with an aza-aromatic N-O-bridged framework, above the Child seed-0 cyclic urea/ether maximum. Child seed 1 changes from Parent 0.19092251395438758 to 0.20101609460096667 with the more aromatic sulfur-substituted family. per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules are exceptionally ring-dense sulfur cages containing nitrogen-rich carbonyl groups, carbon-bound fluorine, alkyl substitution and, in the strongest seed-1 family, an NH-containing dione and a fluorinated alcohol side chain. A brominated ring position varies to chlorine or bromomethyl. The seed-0 cages additionally contain N-Cl, sulfur-fluorine, N-O and sulfur-sulfur multiple-bond connections. Seed 2 produces a partly saturated carbonyl/imino nitrogen framework with N-F and sulfur-containing rings. Final seed-2 structures retain N-F, imino functionality and unusual sulfur-ring bonds, but differ substantially from the displayed strongest dione cage. Every proposal has ring tokens, whereas the aromatic-token rate is 0.7839: this is a mixture of aromatic substructures and heavily nonaromatic ring chemistry. The compact appearance does not imply ordinary synthetic plausibility; bonding and the dense topology are major concerns.
liabilities: Multiply bonded sulfur with additional ring attachments, including sulfur-sulfur triple bonds, is not conventional medicinal sulfur chemistry.
N-F, N-Cl, sulfur-fluorine and N-O connections appear in alternative leading cages and raise reactivity concerns.
Dense fused and bridged ring connections can impose severe geometric constraints that a SMILES string and score do not resolve.

The early ring-expanded aromatic dione scores 7.590554525032884e-10 and a different sulfur-rich cage 1.0546805269255595e-09, so carbonyl groups, sulfur and many rings are plainly insufficient on their own. The observed gradient associates with particular compact fluorinated/carbonyl arrangements; it does not reveal a mandatory absent pharmacophore or validate the cages. Parent and Child remain in fluorinated carbonyl/sulfur families: their seed-1 maxima are 0.5903526424693334 and 0.4978675538217162. Seed-0 maxima are 0.48118636011729826 and 0.47628381509500306, and seed-2 maxima 0.4484554129767839 and 0.4413006791220245. transferable_gaps.evidence: An ordinary indole amide reaches 0.39905049777278273, while other leaders carry N-Cl, O-F, O-O-F and multiply bonded sulfur. A fused-ring carbon/sulfur pair both score 0.9440022868010379; a sulfur-sulfur single/triple-bond pair both score 0.45634604420642844. These recorded ties do not support a requirement for the extra sulfur or bond order.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve useful aromatic, amine and carbonyl arrangements without adding reactive heteroatom bonds or unusual sulfur coordination.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Broaden matched substitutions and linkers with conventional stable bonding while retaining the surrounding fragment placement. Distinguish ordinary sulfur functional groups and carbon-bound halogens from unusual sulfur coordination and reactive heteroatom-halogen connections; let observed feedback determine which alternatives retain the useful arrangement.

transferable_gaps.evidence: N-chloromethyl, N-methyl and N-ethyl amidine relatives share 0.6057957681692732, and an O-O-F relative remains close at 0.6051188299817185. Aryl chlorine/bromine and oxygenated sulfur-link variants also share 0.20101609460096667. The output therefore contains complexity and reactivity that these local observations do not establish as necessary.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically simpler peripheral variants remain incomplete where the recorded score is insensitive to appendage chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Include coherent matched simplifications of side chains and reactive substituents while preserving the principal ring framework and polar-group attachments. Use actual feedback to retain simpler chemistry when it performs similarly, without assuming that deleting arbitrary fragments is beneficial.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Contracting and dearomatizing an N-bound aromatic substituent accompanies a change from 0.9441493227693659 to 0.31720419251336807. Ring-opened carbonyl-chain examples score 0.12467972074136988 and 0.1263981386214515. In parallel, strong molecules repeatedly acquire small fused carbocycles, expanded heterocycles or very dense sulfur cages.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator varies ring connectivity without consistently retaining the spatial organization associated with its stronger molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide matched feasible ring-size, linker-length and attachment variations that preserve the other useful fragments. Expand access to ordinary saturated and aromatic ring arrangements with controlled geometry, rather than equating more closures or retained aromatic tokens with a useful conformation.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has stereocentre-token rate 0.0. The cited products contain substituted saturated nitrogen rings, fluorinated alcohol centres, small fused carbocycles and densely connected cage junctions. Ring-closure rate 1.0 across the proposal sets establishes extensive ring syntax, not an accessible stereoisomer.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereochemical identity and realizable geometry remain unspecified for the constrained products the generator emits.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent feasible configurations when stereogenic relationships arise and preserve their identity through structural changes. Combine configuration handling with geometrically plausible ring alternatives; the current observations do not show that specifying stereochemistry alone would change a score.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.
